name: AI VFX Studio
description: AI VFX Studio turns one still image into a short video using a preset effect: a camera move, an AI transformation or an explosion/element VFX. You pick an effect card, add an image, choose aspect ratio, duration, size and quality, and press Generate.
shortDescription: Hollywood camera moves, explosive VFX and AI effects from a single image.
fullDescription: AI VFX Studio is a native in-app version of the open-source AI-VFX app. The page has an input bar at the top (image box, optional prompt, image URL field, four dropdowns and a Generate button) and a gallery of effect cards underneath, grouped in three tabs: AI Effects (64 presets), Motion Controls (47 camera moves) and VFX (9 elements and destruction effects). Everything runs through the MuAPI generate_wan_ai_effects endpoint, so you need a MuAPI key. Defaults are 9:16 portrait, 5 seconds, 480p and Medium quality, which keeps first tests quick. Finished videos appear in a results grid on the page with a Download link, and are also saved to your generation history.
bestFor: Creators who want fast cinematic camera moves, explosion or elemental VFX and viral-style AI transformations from a single photo, with simple controls for aspect ratio, length and quality.
whenToUse: You have one image and want a ready-made camera move such as Dolly In, Crash Zoom In, 360 Orbit or FPV Drone Cam.
You want an element or destruction effect such as Building Explosion, Tornado, Electricity or Disintegration.
You want a viral-style AI transformation such as Hulk Transformation, Kamehameha or Cakeify.
You want to choose between portrait, landscape and square, and between 5 or 10 second clips.
You want to paste an image link instead of uploading a file.
whenToUseAnother: Use Effects Studio (#/effects) when you want still-image effects (figurines, comic looks, Nano Banana, Kontext edits), the extra Video FX v2 presets, before-and-after compare, or Add to Library and Insert into Timeline buttons.
Use Animate Studio (#/animate) when you want to describe the motion yourself and pick any image-to-video model.
Use Video Tools (#/videotools) when you already have a video and want to upscale, translate, caption or recast it.
Use Video Studio (#/video) for text-to-video or image-to-video with full model selection.
Use Timeline (#/timeline) to assemble several clips into a finished edit.
keyFeatures: Three category tabs with counts: AI Effects (64), Motion Controls (47), VFX (9).
Thumbnail grid of effect cards; click a card to select it.
Image input by upload or by pasting an https image URL.
Optional prompt: describe the subject, for example a red sports car.
Four dropdowns: Aspect, Duration, Size, Quality.
Generate button with live Rendering message and a results grid with Download links.
Results saved to your generation history.

featureExplanations.explanation: While rendering, a card says Rendering and the effect name. When ready a video card appears with playback controls, the effect name and a Download link. New results appear first.

featureExplanations.restrictions: The results grid only holds this visit's results; older ones are in your generation history. There are no Add to Library, Timeline, Compare or Publish buttons on this page.

howToUse: 1. Open AI VFX Studio from the side menu (#/ai-vfx). 2. Choose a tab: AI Effects, Motion Controls or VFX. 3. Click an effect card. The line above the prompt changes from Pick an effect below, add an image, then Generate. to Effect: followed by the effect name. 4. Click the dashed Add image box to upload a picture (JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF), or paste a link in the ...or paste an image URL (https://) field. 5. Optional: type the subject in the prompt box. 6. Set Aspect (9:16 Portrait, 16:9 Landscape, 1:1 Square), Duration (5s or 10s), Size (480p or 720p) and Quality (Medium or High). 7. Press Generate. The button shows Generating... and a card shows Rendering with the effect name. 8. When the toast says Video ready, play the result and press Download.
howToSteps: Add an image by upload or https link.
Choose Aspect, Duration, Size and Quality.
Press Generate and wait for Video ready.
Press Download on the result card.
gettingStarted: Keep the defaults (9:16, 5s, 480p, Medium) for your first test; they render fastest.
Try a Motion Controls move like Dolly In on a clear product or portrait photo.
Once you like the effect, switch Size to 720p and Quality to High for a final render.

inputDetails.restrictions: If empty no prompt is sent.

inputDetails.name: Aspect

modelCapabilities: AI VFX Studio has no model picker. All three tabs call the MuAPI generate_wan_ai_effects endpoint (a Wan-based effects service) through the shared MuAPI client. The AI Effects list comes from the ai-video-effects model definition, Motion Controls from motion-controls and VFX from the vfx model, so every card shown is a name the API accepts. The catalog file describes ai-video-effects as an AI video effects pipeline, motion-controls as motion parameter control for image-to-video, and vfx as visual effects processing. No price, speed or quality numbers for these models appear in the catalog, description or comparison files, so none are stated.
outputs: A short video clip in 9:16, 16:9 or 1:1.
Shown in the results grid with a Download link and saved to your generation history.
limitations: Single image input only; no video or multi-image input.
Preset effects only; no custom effect creation.
Duration options are only 5s and 10s; resolution options only 480p and 720p.
No compare, library, timeline or social-publish buttons on this page.
Requires a MuAPI key; uploads follow MuAPI limits (10 MB for images).
Duplicate-looking names exist across studios (for example Flying also appears in Effects Studio's Video FX v2 tab); each studio uses its own list.

limitationDetails.workaround: Use Upscale tools in Video Tools (#/videotools) to enlarge the finished clip.

limitationDetails.impact: You cannot blend several images into one effect.
limitationDetails.workaround: Use Animate Studio with a reference-style model, or Video Studio.

limitationDetails.impact: You must download the clip to reuse it elsewhere.
limitationDetails.workaround: Use Download, then upload into Timeline or Video Tools. Your history also keeps the generation.

troubleshooting: Toast says Select an effect first: click one of the effect cards, then press Generate.
Toast says Add an image (upload or https URL) first: upload a picture or paste an https link and wait for the thumbnail to appear in the box.
Toast says Image URL must start with http(s)://: paste a full link beginning with https://.
Settings window opens when you upload or generate: add your MuAPI key and try again.
Toast says Upload failed or shows an upload error: check the file is JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF and 10 MB or smaller, then retry.
Toast says No video URL returned: the service finished without a video. Try again, or choose another effect or image.
Generation failed toast (shown for about 6 seconds): read the message, retry, or reduce to the defaults (5s, 480p, Medium).
Image is blank or the preview does not load from a pasted URL: the link may block hotlinking. Download the image and upload it instead.
An effect card shows no thumbnail: the picture is missing but the effect still works.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: Nothing happens when I press Generate
steps: Check the line above the prompt shows Effect: and a name.
Confirm a thumbnail appears in the image box.
Wait: while busy the button reads Generating... and is disabled.
Use JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF.
Keep the file at 10 MB or less.
Make sure your MuAPI key is saved.
Try pasting an image URL instead.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: The effect does not look right
steps: Use a clear, well-composed image with an obvious subject.
Add a short prompt naming the subject.
Switch Quality to High and Size to 720p.
Try a different effect in the same tab.

commonProblems.howToFix: Change Size to 720p and Quality to High.

commonProblems.problem: Portrait video when I wanted landscape
commonProblems.howToFix: Change Aspect to 16:9 Landscape before pressing Generate.

commonProblems.whyItHappens: The prompt is dropped into the effect's template and is only meant to describe the subject.
commonProblems.howToFix: Reword the prompt as a short noun phrase, like a red sports car.

faqs.question: How many effects are there?
faqs.answer: The tabs show AI Effects 64, Motion Controls 47 and VFX 9, so 120 presets. The upstream project text mentions 80+ effects, but the numbers on the tab buttons in this app are the ones to trust.

faqs.question: Can I make a 10 second video?
faqs.answer: Yes. Set Duration to 10s. The default is 5s.

faqs.question: What is the difference between this and Effects Studio?
faqs.answer: AI VFX Studio focuses on video-from-one-image with Aspect, Duration, Size and Quality controls and includes the VFX tab. Effects Studio also has still-image effect tabs, Video FX v2, compare, library, timeline and Advanced settings, but fixes video at 720p and 5 seconds.

faqs.question: Do I need a prompt?
faqs.answer: No. It is optional and is only used to describe the subject.

faqs.question: Which image formats work?
faqs.answer: The uploader accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP and GIF. You can also paste an https image link.

faqs.question: How long does it take?
faqs.answer: The upstream README says typically 1 to 3 minutes. The page itself shows Rendering until the service replies; actual times vary by effect, duration and quality.

faqs.question: Where are my videos kept?
faqs.answer: The results grid shows videos from this visit with a Download link, and each one is saved to your generation history.

glossary.VFX: Visual effects, such as explosions, electricity or levitation.
glossary.Motion Control: A preset camera move such as a dolly, orbit or crane shot.
glossary.Aspect: The shape of the video, such as 9:16 for phones or 16:9 for widescreen.
glossary.MuAPI: The service that renders the effects. A MuAPI key is required.

tips: Test with defaults first, then upgrade to 720p and High for the keeper.
Use sharp, well-lit images with a clear subject.
Match the subject to the effect: car for Car Explosion, person for transformations.
Keep prompts to a few words naming the subject.
bestPractices: Pick Aspect first so you do not need to re-render for a different platform.
Download clips you like right away.
Use short prompts and one effect per render.
